deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is an administrative attendance and discipline sheet from a 'Salle des calculs' (computing room), headed 'Séance du 31 octobre 1857'. The context, the names and the French bureaucratic form strongly suggest the computing bureau of the Paris Observatory under Le Verrier, where Gustave Leveau was a calculator. I am inferring that location; the page does not name it.

The sheet lists the computers present, with their arrival times ('heure d'arrivée'). Only the first entry gives the hour explicitly ('8h.'); the remaining minute values are read as also falling in the 8 o'clock hour (my inference):
- Serret: 8h28
- Boblin: (8h)34
- Leveau: (8h)20
- Delépine: (8h)20
- Vinches: (8h)32
- Monin: (8h)20

Two standard questions follow, each answered 'O.', most likely meaning 'Oui':
- 'Le silence a-t-il été observé?' (Was silence observed?)
- 'Le travail a-t-il été quitté et repris aux heures fixées par le règlement?' (Was work stopped and resumed at the hours fixed by the regulations?)

The sheet is signed 'C. J. Serret' with a paraph (flourish). The pencilled '56' is the archival folio number.

The item is not in Riemann's hand and has no connection to his mathematical work. It is presumably a stray sheet filed in the 'Varia' bundle. The previous page is only show-through from the reverse side, and there is no next page, so there is nothing further to reconstruct.

transcription_corrections: 'réglement' is written as such in the image; this is the period spelling of modern 'règlement', not a transcription error.
'O.' after each question most likely abbreviates 'Oui'; it could also be read as a zero or 'O' mark, but 'Oui' fits the form.
The minute entries 34, 20, 20, 32, 20 are implicitly in the 8 o'clock hour; only Serret's line gives '8h.' explicitly.
Name 'Vinches' is uncertain in the hand (could be 'Vinches' or 'Vincher'); 'Boblin' and 'Monin' also read as transcribed but are not independently verified.
The pencilled '56' at right margin is the archival folio number, not part of the document.
